title: Renewal + Expansion check-in - Aegis Financial
next_steps: Alex to send revised 24-month renewal quote with EU region pricing - due 2027-10-14
Samira to schedule performance benchmark window and provide test harness - due 2027-10-18
Rina to receive SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration notes - due 2027-10-15
Priya to share Q1-Q4 usage forecast and peak QPS targets - due 2027-10-19
action_items: Priya Rao | Share monthly token and embedding usage, and expected growth % | due 2027-10-19
Alex Monroe | Send revised contract with 24-month term and tiered discount + EU region addendum | due 2027-10-14
Samira Patel | Set up dedicated benchmark runs (50k tokens/day sim) and provide test harness repo link | due 2027-10-18
Rina Gupta | Confirm encryption at rest KMS provider and provide SOC2 scoping Q&A answers | due 2027-10-15
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer exploring capacity upgrade from reserved 8-GPU pool to 20 GPUs, adding EU region, and moving from 12 to 24 month contract for better pricing. Key concerns: data residency, KMS integration, SLA for cross-region failover, and demonstration of sustained latency under peak QPS. Agreed next steps: revised quote, benchmark window, security docs, usage forecast.
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
00:10 Priya (Aegis): Hi, Priya here.
00:12 Marcus (Aegis): Marcus on infra.
00:13 Ethan (Aegis): Ethan from procurement.
00:15 Rina (Aegis): Rina security.
00:18 Alex: Awesome, and Samira and Jordan are with me from Redwood, Samira is our solutions engineer.
00:25 Samira (Redwood): Hey all, quick wave.
00:28 Alex: Agenda - run through renewal timeline, capacity ask, region add, security questions, then recap next steps. Sound good?
00:35 Priya: Yep, sounds good.
00:40 Alex: Cool. So Priya, Marcus, last quarter you mentioned hitting higher tail latency during peak batch updates; wanted to get an update on production behavior and what you're thinking for renewal.
00:52 Priya: Yeah, so we've been ramping, usage grew about 2.8x since last renewal, our 95th latency spikes to around 420ms on hosted endpoints, and we saw some queuing at peak which delayed risk-scoring pipelines. That's why we are talking capacity upgrades.
01:10 Marcus: Just to add, our infra team is pushing for isolation - we prefer dedicated capacity for compliance and predictability. The current 8 GPU Reserved pool is getting saturated during month-end runs.
01:22 Alex: Understood. Primary asks then are: bump to ~20 GPUs reserved, add EU region for data residency and failover, and extend contract length to get better unit pricing. Is that accurate?
01:34 Priya: Yes. Also we want to validate cross-region failover SLO and ensure KV cache warm-up isn't adding huge latency on failover.
01:45 Samira: Good point - our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we have a warm-up policy, but for cross-region we need to prove the cold-start behavior. We can run a benchmark simulating failover.
01:58 Rina: And security wise, we need KMS integration details. We, we can't ship keys to a vendor-managed key store; bring-your-own-KMS or HSM preferred. Also SOC2 evidence and audit logs retention for 12 months minimum.
02:12 Jordan (Redwood CSM): We've done BYO-KMS with several customers; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. We'll put the integration notes in the doc we share.
02:24 Ethan: From procurement, pricing - moving from 12-month to 24-month looks viable if discounts are meaningful. What's standard discount band for 24mo?
02:34 Alex: Typically we offer 8-18% depending on commit and capacity. For a jump to 20 GPUs we'd likely be in the 12-15% range plus an add-on for EU region capacity. I'll run numbers and include the breakouts in a quote.
02:47 Marcus: Also curious about burst capacity - some month ends we need temporary +10 GPUs for 48 hours. How does burst work on Dedicated?
02:56 Samira: We support burst pools; can be configured as pre-approved burst capacity with automatic billing at the burst rate, or as negotiated credits. We'll include burst config options in the proposal.
03:08 Priya: On latency, can you share historic tail latency numbers for similar customers on 20-GPU pools? We want to set realistic SLOs.
03:18 Samira: Yes, we have anonymized benchmark profiles. For 20 GPU dedicated with similar seq lengths we typically see 95th under 200-250ms for the text-gen model family we onboarded. But depends on model size and quantization. We'll share the perf deck.
03:34 Priya: Great. Also, we are evaluating Anthropic and running some in-house comparisons; we'd like Redwood to demonstrate sustained throughput under our workload.
03:45 Alex: Totally fair, that's why we propose the benchmark window. We'll coordinate data and scripts.
03:52 Marcus: About EU region - data residency is a must for some product lines. We need the EU control plane or at least EU data plane and logs stored in EU. Does Redwood provide EU-only data flow for Private?
04:06 Jordan: For Redwood Private yes, you can choose region placement. For Hosted/Dedicated we have options to pin to EU region and we can add contractual data residency language. There are slight operational differences for Private vs Dedicated hosted variants; we'll capture that in the addendum.
04:22 Rina: Also need encryption at rest, TLS 1.3, VPC peering or PrivateLink options, and SAML SSO mapping for RBAC.
04:32 Samira: All supported: TLS 1.3 by default, SAML SSO supported, RBAC role mapping, and VPC peering/PrivateLink for network isolation. We'll attach the network setup guide.
04:44 Ethan: From legal side, any changes to indemnity or data processing addendum with the region add-on?
04:50 Alex: The DPA will include region clauses; no major changes to indemnities but we'll confirm with legal.
04:57 Priya: For the benchmark, we want three windows: baseline (current 8 GPUs), scaled (20 GPUs), and failover simulation switching EU<->US to measure KV cold starts. Each window should be 4-6 hours overnight. Can Redwood run that?
05:12 Samira: Yes, we can. We'll need the test harness and sample prompts; preferably a representative subset not PII. We'll coordinate with Priya's team on data sanitization.
05:24 Priya: We'll scrub samples. Also need guidance on quantization tradeoffs — we want cost savings without hurting prediction quality.
05:33 Samira: We can test int8 quantized variants; Redwood Optimize recommends profiles by workload. We'll include suggested quantization profiles and expected cost savings.
05:44 Priya: Perf question - does the runtime maintain per-request KV cache across models if we do mixed-model routing? We have a mixed stack for reranking then generation.
05:56 Samira: KV cache is model-specific; when routing between compatible model variants we can preserve cache, but across different architectures it won't. If you use a model family variant we can preserve some cache. We'll diagram that in the benchmark notes.
06:12 Marcus: On monitoring - we need per-route token-level cost breakdowns and trace hooks forwarded to our observability stack. Can we integrate with Datadog and our tracing?
06:23 Jordan: Yes, Datadog and OpenTelemetry tracing hooks are supported. We'll share the integration guide and standard dashboards.
06:30 Priya: Any downtime during migration or region add? We prefer zero-downtime but expect some planned maintenance windows.
06:38 Alex: For Dedicated and Private we aim for rolling upgrades with minimal impact; for cross-region replication initial sync for KV may cause a short warm-up but not complete downtime. We'll outline the runbook.
06:50 Ethan: Back to pricing - if we commit to 24 months and prepay some portion, what's the best effective rate?
06:58 Alex: Prepaying 6-months or annual reduces rate further; I'll model scenarios: 24mo net with 12mo prepaid, 24mo net with no prepay, and 12mo renewal for comparison.
07:12 Rina: For audit logs retention, we need immutable logs for 12 months and exportable for eDiscovery. Is that possible?
07:20 Jordan: Yes, logs can be exported to customer S3/GCS in the EU region, with retention policies. We'll include the export steps.
07:28 Priya: Okay, tentative timeline: renewal effective date in ~45 days. We need the quote within 48 hours, benchmark within next week, security docs in three days. Is that realistic?
07:40 Alex: Yes. We'll aim to get the quote by 2027-10-14, security docs by 2027-10-15, and schedule benchmarks for next week (2027-10-18 to 2027-10-20).
07:52 Marcus: One more question: in case of capacity shortage, what are fallback policies? Auto-scaling to hosted, or throttling?
08:02 Samira: Smart routing supports fallback to compatible hosted variants or lower-capacity quantized models. For mission-critical flows we recommend pre-authorized burst capacity to avoid throttling.
08:14 Priya: Will we get automatic model rollback on regressions? We had an issue with a model update last quarter.
08:21 Jordan: Rollouts support canary and automatic rollback based on quality regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll show the rollout UI and how to pin model versions.
08:33 Ethan: Procurement question: do we need a PO or standard contract signature?
08:37 Alex: Either works; we accept PO with attached SOW or e-signed agreement. We'll send both options.
08:43 Rina: Clarify KMS - we use an on-prem HSM for key custody, are there customers running HSM with Redwood Private?
08:51 Samira: Yes, we've integrated with customer HSMs over PKCS#11 and via cloud HSM bridged setups for Private. For Dedicated we can do BYO-KMS in many cases. We'll include the integration case studies.
09:05 Priya: Great. Anything else?
09:07 Alex: Not from us. Quick recap: Alex to send revised quote with pricing bands and EU addendum; Samira to schedule and run three benchmark windows and share harness; Jordan to send network and logging integration docs; Rina to get SOC2 artifacts; Priya to share usage forecast.
09:28 Priya: Yes, we'll aim to turn around the forecast and the scrubbed sample data by the due dates.
09:33 Alex: Sweet. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and post notes in the shared workspace.
09:38 Ethan: Thanks.
09:40 Marcus: Thanks all.
09:42 Rina: Bye.
09:44 Samira: Bye.
09:46 End of recording.
